newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union-Preston leap-frogs Tonu'u at halfback.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Preston leap-frogs Tonu'u at halfback.

text.p: AUCKLAND, May 20 - Wellington Hurricanes halfback Jon Preston on Friday left for Saturday night's Super 12 rugby semifinal against ACT in Canberra bolstered by the knowledge that he is now the second best halfback in New Zealand, NZPA reports.
All Black coach John Hart said as much when he today named the New Zealand Barbarians and New Zealand A teams for the June 8 trial in Rotorua.
The announcement of the teams shows that Preston has now clearly leap-frogged Auckland's Ofisa Tonu'u as the back up for test halfback Justin Marshall.
Preston was named in the reserves of the shadow test side, the Barbarians, while Tonu'u will start opposite Marshall in the New Zealand A team.
"Jon Preston's selection in the reserves signifies that we now see him as the second best halfback in the country," Hart said in naming the trial teams at Albany today.
"I think last year we said he was our third best halfback and maybe our fourth best first five-eighth and a super-sub.
"I think his form this year has dramatically improved at halfback and he deserves his spot on the basis of his performance."
Preston's Hurricanes' team-mate, the giant dreadlocked winger Tana Umaga, also gained the nod in the shadow test team reserves and will get game time in Rotorua.
"His form as a winger has been a stand out, we think he has developed tremendously in 1997. In 1996 he had a lot of work to do, and he's done that," Hart said.

"We have been impressed with his professionalism on and off the field and the way he has taken the challenge. Clearly in the trial we will be looking to get him on the field and it is great to see another form player come into trial contention."

Otago's Taine Randell has fulfilled all the goals the selectors have set for him and offers cover in the trial in all three looseforward positions while Waikato's Scott McLeod offers the same option at second five-eighth, centre and wing.
In the New Zealand A team Hart paid tribute to Auckland centre Eroni Clarke.

"Clarke has progressed this year to be a genuine test centre contender. His inclusion this year, particularly that he has now leap-frogged a couple of players that may have been seen ahead of him, is based on his excellent form," Hart said.
Hart also singled out Canterbury's Steve Surridge as a bolter who has come to national prominence as a future No 8 contender in front of the likes of Waikato's Deon Muir and Wellington's Filo Tiatia.
"He has been one of the real comers of the season, he has had injuries but has played quite outstandingly for the Crusaders this season," Hart said.
"He represents a lot of the skill sets required under the new rules particularly in terms of speed and vision at No 8."

The All Black selectors also made the encouraging move of selecting youngsters such as Auckland's 22-year-old prop Paul Thomson, Canterbury's first-five eighth Leon McDonald, Waikato halfback Mark Robinson and Northland lock Norm Maxwell in the New Zealand A squad.
The Barbarians will be coached by the All Black management while the New Zealand A side will be coached by Canterbury's Wayne Smith and his offsider Peter Sloane.
The 1996 All Blacks to miss out on selection are veteran prop Phil Coffin, Waikato fullback Matthew Cooper, Canterbury centre Tabai Matson and Southland first five-eighth Simon Culhane.
Teams:-

NZ Barbarians: Christian Cullen, Jeff Wilson, Frank Bunce, Glen Osborne, Lee Stensness, Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall, Zinzan Brooke, Josh Kronfeld, Ian Jones, Robin Brooke, Charles Riechelmann, Craig Dowd, Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), Olo Brown.
Reserves: Jon Preston, Scott McLeod, Tana Umaga, Mark Allen, Norm Hewitt, Taine Randell.

New Zealand A: Adrian Cashmore, James Kerr, Eroni Clarke, Eric Rush, Mark Mayerhofler, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Steve Surridge, Mark Carter, Mark Cooksley, Glenn Taylor, Todd Blackadder (captain), Paul Thomson, Anton Oliver, Con Barrell.
Reserves: Darryl Lilley, Jeremy Stanley, Leon McDonald, Mark Robinson, Shane McDonald, Norm Maxwell, Kee Meeuws, Andrew Blowers.
Players not considered: Michael Jones, Walter Little, Alama Ieremia, Chresten Davis, Jonah Lomu, Blair Larsen, Joeli Vidiri, Dylan Mika.
